citeAs: Pranav Rajpurkar, Jian Zhang, Konstantin Lopyrev, Percy Liang (2016). SQuAD: 100,000+ Questions for Machine Comprehension of Text.
creator: Pranav Rajpurkar, Jian Zhang, Konstantin Lopyrev, Percy Liang (Stanford University)
description: A reading comprehension dataset consisting of 100,000+ questions posed by crowdworkers on a set of Wikipedia articles, where the answer to each question is a segment of text from the corresponding reading passage.
name: Stanford Question Answering Dataset (SQuAD)
rai:annotationsPerItem: Up to 5 questions per paragraph. For the development and test sets, at least 2 additional answers were obtained for each question.
rai:annotatorDemographics: Crowdworkers located in the United States or Canada, with a 97% HIT acceptance rate and a minimum of 1000 HITs.
rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Human performance was evaluated based on inter-annotator agreement, achieving 77.0% for exact match and 86.8% for F1 on the test set. Mismatch occurs mostly due to inclusion/exclusion of non-essential phrases.
rai:dataAnnotationPlatform: Daemo platform, with Amazon Mechanical Turk as its backend
rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Crowdworkers were tasked with asking and answering up to 5 questions on the content of a paragraph. Questions were entered in a text field, and answers highlighted in the paragraph. Tasks contained a sample paragraph and examples of good/bad questions. Workers were encouraged to use their own words, reinforced by disabling copy-paste functionality. Secondary workers selected the shortest span answering the question or marked it unanswerable.
rai:dataCollection: Used Project Nayuki’s Wikipedia’s internal PageRanks to obtain the top 10000 articles of English Wikipedia, sampled 536 articles uniformly at random, and extracted individual paragraphs.
rai:dataCollectionMissingData: If a question was not answerable by a span in the paragraph, workers were asked to submit the question without marking an answer. Over the development and test sets, 2.6% of questions were marked unanswerable by at least one additional crowdworker.
rai:dataCollectionRawData: Top 10000 articles of English Wikipedia based on Project Nayuki’s internal PageRanks.
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Extracted individual paragraphs from Wikipedia articles, stripping away images, figures, tables, and discarding paragraphs shorter than 500 characters.
rai:dataUseCases: Reading comprehension and open-domain question answering.
rai:machineAnnotationTools: Stanford CoreNLP was used to generate constituency parses, POS tags, and NER tags to automatically categorize answers.
